card: Adds the WalletBalanceManySpent benchmark to measure GetBalance execution time on wallets holding tens of thousands of spent outputs and few unspent coins, simulating exchange hot wallets and Lightning nodes. It also extracts fake block generation helpers into a shared benchmark utility header. The benchmark was created to profile and evaluate optimizations in PR 27865 that separate spent transaction outputs from spendable ones.
changed_since_previous: The pull request is no longer draft, and the diff implementation is now available; the functional scope and approach are unchanged.
evidence: The PR description states it was created to test #27865 ('Track no-longer-spendable TXOs separately') and that 'this pattern mirrors real-world usage in high-activity wallets such as Lightning nodes, exchanges, hot wallets, and payment processors.'
problem: Wallet benchmarks lacked coverage for high-activity wallet usage patterns where the vast majority of historical transaction outputs have already been spent, such as in Lightning nodes, payment processors, or exchange hot wallets. Developers had no benchmark to profile or measure the performance of balance calculations under this workload or evaluate optimizations that track spent outputs separately.

risk.why: Touches only benchmark code and benchmark helper utilities with no effect on production code.

scope_notes: Mechanically extracts and parameterizes `generateFakeBlock` from `src/bench/wallet_create_tx.cpp` into a new inline header `src/bench/wallet_bench_util.h`.
summary: Adds the `WalletBalanceManySpent` benchmark to measure `GetBalance()` runtime on wallets with large histories consisting mostly of spent outputs (50,000 created outputs, 49,950 spent, 50 unspent). Also extracts fake block generation helpers from `wallet_create_tx.cpp` into a reusable header `bench/wallet_bench_util.h` for synthetic wallet block generation without full validation.
